The people are invented and long dead, except the three living ones at the end, who show how the living are drawn: by relationship and place, with no dates, and a child by an initial.
title: Down from Valmora
eyebrow: The story · three generations · Valmora to Port Alder
dek: An invented family, told once as a short book: a weaver on a hill, a ship, a harbour town.

paragraphs.text: This is the short version of a long archive: three generations of one family, told in order. Every paragraph says how well it is known.

paragraphs.text: On 4 March 1790 the priest of Valmora baptised a boy, [Tomas Arden](person:tomas-arden-1790), son of a weaver. The register gives the trade of the father and nothing of the mother's family.
Valmora lay in the county of Hollin, a day's walk from the river. The weavers of such hill villages worked wool from the common pasture and sold their cloth at the autumn fair.

evidence.why: General history of the hill weavers

paragraphs.tbc: The fair's date is from a regional history, not from a document about this village.

paragraphs.text: The family says the first Arden came over the pass with his loom on his back. No paper says so.

chapters.title: Down to the sea

paragraphs.text: By the census of 1851 a shipwright called Pieter Arden, aged twenty-nine, lived at Port Alder with a wife, Greta, and two small children. The archive reads him as the boy of 1822 from Valmora, and says so plainly: it is inference.
paragraphs.tbc: The identification of the shipwright with the boy of 1822 is still inference.

paragraphs.text: Port Alder in those years was a harbour of some forty ships and a population that doubled in a generation; the archive's own page on the harbour lists the yards.

evidence.why: The archive's page on the harbour

quote.title: The census
quote.text: Arden, Pieter, 29, shipwright; Greta, 25; Jan, 2; Lise, infant.

chapters.hardLimit: The census gives an age, not a birthplace; Valmora is the archive's reading.

paragraphs.text: Jan's great-grandson Rowan lives at Port Alder with his wife Mira. By this archive's rule the living are named with their relationships and their towns and nothing more; their daughter, by her initial only.

evidence.why: The direct line, the last generation, as the archive publishes it

unknown.title: What we do not know
unknown.lead: Every chapter has its silences. These are the ones a single letter or an afternoon in a reading room could break.

items.text: **Whether the shipwright of 1851 is the boy of 1822.** A Valmora burial or a Port Alder marriage naming the father would settle it.
